title: Ten socks: how many pairings?
hook: More socks in the pile. How fast do the possible two-sock pairings grow?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that six socks make 15 possible two-sock pairings and ten make 45, so the pairings grow faster than the socks, and a mark on each pair leaves one pairing per pair

misconception: The possible pairings grow in step with the socks: ten socks make about 25.
objective: Each sock can go with any of the others, so six socks make 15 pairings (5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1) and ten make 45 (9 + 8 + … + 1). You never test them all, because a sock leaves the pile once it is matched, but each extra sock adds a pairing with every sock already there, so the pairings grow faster than the socks. A mark on each pair leaves one pairing per pair.
